abstract: Validates sensory and physical fitness assessments for high-tonnage all-weather pilotage
system_message:
You are the Maritime Medical Examiner (MME), responsible for validating sensory and physical fitness assessments for high-tonnage all-weather pilotage, as well as monitoring physical endurance qualifications across pilot candidates.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Validates sensory and physical fitness assessments for high-tonnage all-weather pilotage（MED）
information_points.content:
MME-MED-HOA：According to the most recent statutory biennial medical review recorded in the ophthalmic clinical assessment card, Captain Helena Vance holds formal medical clearance for unassisted night navigation and chromatic aid detection, confirming that night vision acuity is certified.
MME-MED-3QC：Based on the most recent statutory biennial medical review documented on the ophthalmic clinical assessment card, Captain Marcus O'Connell has received formal medical clearance for unassisted night navigation and chromatic aid detection, confirming that night vision acuity is certified.
MME-MED-BLF：The most recent statutory biennial medical review documented in the ophthalmic clinical assessment card indicates that Captain Tariq Al-Mansoor does not hold formal medical clearance for unassisted night navigation and chromatic aid detection, meaning night vision acuity is not certified.

information_points.title: Physical endurance monitoring（FIT）
information_points.content:
MME-FIT-4XY：Under the triennial pilot physical examination cycle from the occupational cardiology assessment, Captain Marcus O'Connell registered a pilot ladder ascent endurance score of 85 points during the standardized cardiac recovery assessment following a 9-meter vertical ladder climb.
MME-FIT-B5V：In the triennial pilot physical examination cycle documented by the occupational cardiology assessment, Captain Helena Vance achieved a standardized cardiac recovery score following a 9-meter vertical ladder climb of 95 points for the pilot ladder ascent endurance score.
MME-FIT-H9A：During the triennial pilot physical examination cycle evaluated in the occupational cardiology assessment, Captain Tariq Al-Mansoor attained a pilot ladder ascent endurance score of 75 points on the standardized cardiac recovery test following a 9-meter vertical ladder climb.
